title: Reverse array using pointers
instructorPromptText: Write a function `void reverse_array(int *arr, int size)` that reverses the elements of an integer array in place using pointer arithmetic (no array indexing like `arr[i]`).

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program strictly use pointer arithmetic (e.g., `*(arr + i)` or incrementing pointers) instead of array indexing syntax (`arr[i]`)?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Forcing pointer usage directly tests the student's understanding of pointers as memory addresses rather than just array aliases.

specGateDimensions.description: Is the reversal performed in-place (with O(1) auxiliary space) using a temporary swap variable, or does it allocate memory?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Memory efficiency is a core reason to use pointers in C; identifying whether the student avoids extra allocations is a key learning indicator.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the function check for a NULL pointer or a size <= 0 to prevent segmentation faults?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Robust systems programming in C requires defensive programming against NULL pointers and invalid boundaries.

expectedDivergences.pattern: Student uses square bracket array indexing (e.g., `arr[i]`) in their code, violating the explicit constraint.
Student fails to check for a NULL pointer before dereferencing, potentially causing a crash.
Student allocates a new array using `malloc` to store the reversed elements instead of swapping in-place.
Student implements the reversal using two pointers (a `start` pointer and an `end` pointer) incrementing/decrementing them until they meet.
Student incorrectly updates pointers or goes out of bounds by 1 due to an off-by-one error on the array size.
